summary: OlympusTrail is a Mars exploration planning tool focused on Arcadia Planitia. It brings together Mars terrain, ice consistency, temperature, dust, sunlight related, and contextual radiation data to help users explore three mission planning questions: where a potential base site may be worth investigating, how a rover or crew might travel under resource and terrain constraints, and what decision points matter if a planned journey becomes infeasible. Its interactive map, site ranking tools, route planner, and AI Guide turn complex geospatial layers into an accessible planning experience. OlympusTrail is a research and educational decision support prototype, not a certified mission planning or crew safety system.
details:
OlympusTrail is an interactive Mars exploration map and planning prototype built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map.” The project focuses on Arcadia Planitia and combines multiple geospatial and environmental datasets into map layers and planning tools.

The application is designed around three related tasks. First, it helps users compare candidate base site locations using available terrain and ice consistency information. Second, it computes terrain aware routes subject to configurable mission constraints such as slope, temperature, local time scenario, oxygen budget, battery energy, and reserve. Third, it presents route outcomes, resource metrics, warnings, and turn back checkpoints so users can understand when a requested journey is infeasible or when returning should be considered.

The backend provides APIs for site ranking, terrain data, route planning, shelter candidate display, and briefing data. The route planner searches a regional grid and returns route status, path geometry, resource estimates, and explanatory details. The frontend uses an interactive map to display the regional data and planning outputs. The AI Guide accepts typed or supported browser speech questions, parses supported requests, calls the planner, and explains planner results in plain language. If Gemini is unavailable, the guide has keyword/template fallbacks.

The project is intended to make planetary data easier to explore and to demonstrate how multiple datasets can inform early stage mission planning discussions. Its outputs are exploratory and depend on the quality, coverage, resolution, and assumptions of the underlying datasets and mission parameters.
